## Where is demand strongest—and what should the owner do next?

I use five years of daily menu-item sales for **R07 in Minneapolis** to answer three practical questions: what sells most, when demand changes, and which relationships are worth investigating.

## Follow the analysis

- **[Data](data.qmd)** — the source tables used and how they connect.
- **[Exploration](eda.qmd)** — understand the sales rows, establish quantity baselines, compare groups, and choose charts based on the question.
- **[Analysis report](report.qmd)** — the business story, relevant graphs, and practical takeaways.
- **[Modeling](modeling.qmd)** — predicting daily demand with tidymodels: two recipes, five workflows, and a full assessment (test, cross-validation, and a time-based split).
- **[Slides](slides.qmd)** — a concise presentation of the main findings.

## The story in brief

**What sells:** drinks and a small group of familiar items account for much of the recorded volume.

**When it sells:** demand rises into summer, and daily patterns vary by weekday and category.

**What is worth testing:** promotions differ by category; weather and marketing show associations that need careful interpretation; price and preparation time show little overall linear relationship with average item-day quantity.

The report uses the graph types covered in Weeks 1–5, including ranking bars, lines, distributions, scatterplots, correlation displays, and faceting, and stays within descriptive analysis. The [Modeling](modeling.qmd) page is the Stage 2 extension: it applies the Weeks 8–12 tidymodels lessons to predict daily demand and assesses every model against simple baselines before recommending one.

| Weeks 1–3 | Getting started, basic and advanced manipulations | [Data](data.qmd) page and [Exploration](eda.qmd) steps 1–4 | The eight joined source tables, data-quality checks, and the daily demand table |

| Week 10 | Making predictions | [Modeling](modeling.qmd) — Week 10 section | Test-set predictions, predicted-vs-actual charts, and residuals over time |
| Weeks 11–12 | Model assessment and interpretation | [Modeling](modeling.qmd) — assessment section | One ranked table (test + CV + time split), lasso penalty tuning, and a named winning model |
| Week 15 | Communicating results | [Slides](slides.qmd) | The presentation of what was learned and what was implemented |
